Subject: Call recap: Performance SLOs & autoscaling next steps

Thanks again for your time today, Samantha — great conversation.

Recap of the requirements we discussed and the items we agreed to validate:

- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end for user-facing text generation <= 300ms (streaming enabled); p99 <= 750ms for spikes.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state 200 req/s, target concurrency ~50 active streams; expected burst to 500 req/s for up to 2 minutes during marketing events.
- Streaming: client needs chunked streaming for partial token rendering and early user feedback.
- Autoscale expectations: desired scale-up time <= 90s to reach burst capacity; warm pool to keep ~10-20% of peak capacity to reduce cold starts; queueing allowed up to 30s with graceful degradation.
- Fallbacks: model downgrade to a cheaper quantized variant when warm pool exhausted, plus queue >30s triggers degraded but functional responses.

Action items (owner -> due):
- Marissa: share our MLP on autoscale behavior + warm pool sizing (attached).
- Dylan: run a quick throughput model with the sample profile you shared and report expected scale-up times (EOD Fri).
- Samantha/Rajesh: confirm whether 30s queue timeout is acceptable and whether there are hard SLA cutoffs for paid users.

Attachments: SLO-Mutual-Action-Plan.pdf, redwood-autoscale-data-sheet.pdf

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync next week with your infra team to walk through warm pool sizing and a quick load test. I'm free Tue/Wed afternoon PT. Let me know what works.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful.

A few clarifications from our side:
- The 300ms p95 is for the end-user render including streaming header; we can accept up to 1s for p99 during spikes but need p95 to be very consistent.
- The 2-minute burst duration is accurate but can spike to 5 minutes in extreme cases (rare). Can your warm pool handle 5-minute events without significant cost blowup?
- Queueing: 30s sounds okay as an upper bound, but for paid customers we need <10s for 99% of requests. We may accept degraded responses beyond that window.

I'll loop in Rajesh (infra) and request a 30-minute slot for Tue afternoon PT. He'll confirm availability.

Subject: Re: Call recap: Performance SLOs & autoscaling next steps

Appreciate the clarifications — good notes.

Quick answers:
- Warm pool: we can configure warm pools to cover 20-30% of expected peak; cost trade-off is linear with reserved warm capacity. For your expected peak (500 req/s burst) we recommend a warm pool sized for ~150-200 req/s to hit the 90s scale-up target and minimize cold starts.
- 5-minute bursts: yes, warm pools can sustain 5-minute events. After warm pool exhaustion we rely on scale-up; our empirical tests (attached streaming-latency-chart.png) show p95 stays <350ms for sustained bursts when warm pool is sized as recommended, p99 under 900ms.
- Queueing behavior: default queue timeout is 30s; we can set per-route timeouts and prioritized queues for paid-tier traffic (priority bump + route pinning). For your paid users' 99% <10s requirement, we recommend a small reserved capacity lane (can be achieved via route isolation or tenant-weighted warm pool).

Attaching:
- SLO-Mutual-Action-Plan.pdf (updated with warm pool numbers)
- redwood-autoscale-data-sheet.pdf
- streaming-latency-chart.png

- Dylan will run a targeted load profile (we have your sample) and send results by EOD Mon.
- Can you confirm Rajesh's availability Tue 2:00–2:30pm PT? If confirmed, I'll send a calendar invite and a short runbook for the load test.
